name: Crawler Crane
instructions: omr/instructions/42042-1-1.pdf (one book, 240 pages; the functions are photographed on pages 234-235: the four levers A-D, and what each does)

functions.does: The Power Functions L motor at the back of the superstructure runs the gearbox: a 24 tooth clutch gear on its shaft drives a 24 tooth gear, and rows of 16 tooth clutch gears carry the turn across the gearbox, one pair (one turning each way) beside each of the four driving rings.
functions.source: book: the gearbox steps (gearbox, gearbox2-4 sub-assemblies) and the motor fitted; page 234 (the motor and battery box, top left)
functions.note: the motor (p673 99499) turns the 24 tooth clutch gear p587 76019, which meshes p586 3648b on the control's shaft; the motor's shaft is on the frame in the model, so the control is the shaft it drives

functions.does: Lever B: with its driving ring pushed one way or the other, the motor drives both tracks together, forward or back: the shaft runs forward through two universal joints to a 12 tooth bevel gear on a vertical shaft down through the turntable's centre, then back under the crawler to an 8 tooth gear on a cross axle that turns the 24 tooth gears on both rear sprockets.
functions.source: book: page 234 (the levers, B with its icon), page 235 (picture B, the crane driving); the drive gears in the crawler and drivegear sub-assemblies
functions.note: the ring is slid as the lever would slide it; sliding it the other way (-10) drives the tracks the other way; unsure which part of the lever assembly is lever B's handle

functions.does: Lever C: the motor slews the superstructure round on the crawler: the driving ring's shaft turns an 8 tooth gear, a 24 tooth clutch gear and a shaft forward to an 8 tooth gear, a 24 tooth gear and a 20 tooth bevel gear, and a 12 tooth gear at the front meshes the turntable's teeth.
functions.source: book: page 234 (the levers, C), page 234 picture C (the superstructure slewing)
functions.note: the ring is slid as the lever would slide it; -10 slews the other way. The slewing moves the crawler (body of p132) against the superstructure (the frame)

functions.does: Lever A: the motor raises and lowers the boom: the driving ring's shaft turns a 20 tooth bevel gear that drives a 12 tooth bevel gear on the worm's shaft, the worm turns the boom winch's drum, and its cables pull the boom up through the pulleys on the A-frame.
functions.source: book: page 234 (the levers, A, and picture A, the boom raised and lowered); winch2 sub-assembly, boompull steps
functions.note: the ring is slid as the lever would slide it; -10 lowers. The boom (p906 and the boom sections) pivots on the superstructure as its cables are wound; unsure which way winds

functions.does: Lever D: the motor raises and lowers the grab: the driving ring's shaft turns a 20 tooth bevel gear, a 12 tooth bevel gear and a worm, which winds the hoist winch's drum; the string runs up the boom over the pulley at its tip and down to the grab.
functions.source: book: page 234 (the levers, D), page 235 picture D (the grab lowered); winch sub-assembly, boomtip and grabbertop steps
functions.note: the ring is slid as the lever would slide it; -10 the other way. The grab hangs on the string

functions.does: The four levers on the superstructure (two pairs) each slide one driving ring forward or back, between its two clutch gears: forward drives its function one way, back the other way, and in the middle it's in neutral.
functions.source: book: the controlsticks sub-assemblies; page 234 (the levers A-D with their arrows and icons)
functions.note: unsure how the model's lever parts map to A-D: by the model, each stick (p829, p840) carries a changeover catch between two rings, and p838 32054 sits on a third pivot

functions.does: The black knob gear on top of the grab opens and closes its four claws: it turns a 20 tooth bevel gear and a 12 tooth bevel gear on a small linear actuator, whose piston pushes the claws' arms.
functions.source: book: page 235 (top right: the knob turned, the claws open); grabber steps
book: page 235 (top middle, the door swung open)

functions.does: The tracks run round their sprockets and rollers when driven.
functions.source: book: the crawler steps (rollers and tread)

functions.does: The spare boom section can be fitted into the boom to make it 12 cm longer.
functions.source: book: pages 226-233 (the extra section), page 235 (bottom right)
functions.note: a building option, not a working function; the model file builds the boom with it fitted (its boomext sub-assemblies)
